Infection Prevention and Control at Home

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of bed making in nursing care?

choices.text: To promote patient comfort, cleanliness and safety
To prevent patients from moving independently
To reduce the need for regular patient assessment
To make the room appear attractive only

questions.rationale: Bed making promotes comfort, cleanliness and a safe environment for the patient. It also provides an opportunity to inspect the mattress and linen for moisture, contamination and other hazards.

questions.question_text: Which type of bed is prepared for a patient who is able to get out of bed independently?

choices.text: Closed bed
Open bed
Occupied bed
Post-operative bed

questions.rationale: An open bed is prepared to receive a patient who is ambulant or able to get into bed independently. The top linen is arranged to allow easy access.

questions.question_text: Which position is commonly used to facilitate examination of the anterior surface of the body?

choices.text: Prone position
Supine position
Lithotomy position
Sims' position

questions.rationale: The supine position involves lying flat on the back with the face directed upwards. It allows access to the anterior surface of the body for many physical examinations and procedures.

questions.question_text: Which position is commonly used to facilitate rectal examination and some nursing procedures involving the perineal area?

choices.text: Sims' position
Supine position
High Fowler's position
Trendelenburg position

questions.rationale: Sims' position is a lateral position in which the patient lies partly on the side, usually with the upper leg flexed. It provides access to the rectal area for selected examinations and procedures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is generally considered a normal resting pulse rate for a healthy adult?

choices.text: 40–50 beats per minute
60–100 beats per minute
110–130 beats per minute
140–160 beats per minute

questions.rationale: The normal resting heart rate for most healthy adults is approximately 60–100 beats per minute. Interpretation should also consider the patient's symptoms, physical condition and medications.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used to measure body temperature?

choices.text: Sphygmomanometer
Thermometer
Stethoscope
Pulse oximeter

questions.rationale: A thermometer measures body temperature. Different types include digital, tympanic and other clinical thermometers, each used according to the manufacturer's instructions and appropriate infection prevention measures.

questions.question_text: What is the term for an abnormally rapid respiratory rate?

choices.text: Bradypnoea
Apnoea
Tachypnoea
Orthopnoea

questions.rationale: Tachypnoea refers to an abnormally increased respiratory rate. It may occur in conditions such as fever, pneumonia, pain, anxiety and respiratory distress.

questions.question_text: Which nursing procedure involves cleaning the entire body of a patient who cannot bathe independently?

choices.text: Oral hygiene
Bed bath
Foot care
Perineal care

questions.rationale: A bed bath is the process of bathing a patient who is unable to use a bathroom or bathe independently. It promotes cleanliness, comfort, skin integrity and observation of the patient's physical condition.

questions.question_text: Which practice is most important before and after providing direct patient care?

choices.text: Changing the patient's clothes
Hand hygiene
Opening all windows
Measuring the patient's height

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is a fundamental infection prevention measure that reduces the transmission of microorganisms. It should be performed at the appropriate moments before and after patient contact and after exposure to potentially infectious materials.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a nasogastric tube?

choices.text: To provide access to the stomach for enteral feeding or medication administration when indicated
To measure blood pressure continuously
To drain urine from the bladder
To administer oxygen directly into the lungs

questions.rationale: A nasogastric tube passes through the nose into the stomach and may be used for enteral feeding, medication administration or gastric decompression. Its use requires appropriate assessment and confirmation of tube position before feeding or medication administration.

questions.question_text: Which device is commonly used to collect urine from a male patient who is unable to walk to the toilet but can urinate voluntarily?

choices.text: Bedpan
Urinal
Nasogastric tube
Suction catheter

questions.rationale: A urinal is designed to collect urine from a patient who can void voluntarily but cannot easily access a toilet. It supports comfort, privacy and monitoring of urine output.

questions.question_text: Which type of urinary catheter remains in the bladder for continuous drainage and is retained by an inflated balloon?

choices.text: Intermittent catheter
Indwelling catheter
External male catheter
Nasogastric catheter

questions.rationale: An indwelling urinary catheter is retained in the bladder by an inflated balloon and connected to a drainage system. It should be used only when clinically indicated because prolonged use increases the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infection.

questions.topic: Admission and Discharge Procedures in Community Care
questions.question_text: Which document provides a formal summary of a patient's diagnosis, treatment and instructions when leaving a health facility?

choices.text: Discharge summary
Staff attendance register
Ward duty roster
Inventory register

questions.rationale: A discharge summary communicates important information about the patient's admission, diagnosis, treatment and continuing care needs. It supports continuity of care between the hospital, patient, family and community health services.

questions.topic: Infection Prevention and Control at Home
questions.question_text: Which term describes the destruction or removal of many pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects, although bacterial spores may remain?

choices.text: Disinfection
Sterilisation
Nutrition
Immunisation

questions.rationale: Disinfection reduces or eliminates many pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects and surfaces. Sterilisation is a more comprehensive process that destroys or removes all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores.

questions.question_text: Which term describes the process of tissue repair that occurs after a wound?

choices.text: Wound healing
Haemorrhage
Necrosis
Maceration

questions.rationale: Wound healing is the biological process through which damaged tissue is repaired. It involves overlapping phases of haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and tissue remodelling.

questions.question_text: Which action is most appropriate for preventing falls among patients with impaired mobility at home?

choices.text: Keep walking areas clear and ensure adequate lighting
Encourage patients to walk without assistance
Place loose rugs near the patient's bed
Keep frequently used items out of reach

questions.rationale: Clear walking areas and adequate lighting reduce environmental hazards that contribute to falls. Additional measures include appropriate footwear, mobility aids and assistance based on individual fall risk.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is preparing an occupied bed for a patient who cannot get out of bed. Which action should the nurse take?

choices.text: Remove all linen at once while leaving the patient uncovered
Explain the procedure, maintain privacy and turn the patient safely to one side while changing the linen
Ask the patient to stand regardless of their condition
Place soiled linen on the floor before disposal

questions.rationale: An occupied bed is made while the patient remains in bed, requiring safe turning and careful handling of linen. Privacy, comfort, body alignment and prevention of contamination should be maintained throughout the procedure.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse discovers that the bedsheets of a bedridden patient are wet with urine. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Allow the linen to dry while the patient remains on it
Change the wet linen, clean and dry the skin, and assess for skin irritation
Cover the wet area with another blanket
Apply powder over the wet bedsheet

questions.rationale: Wet linen increases moisture exposure and the risk of skin irritation and pressure injury. Changing the linen and providing appropriate skin care help maintain skin integrity and comfort.

questions.question_text: A patient with difficulty breathing is being cared for at home. Which position is most appropriate to help ease breathing?

choices.text: Flat supine position
High Fowler's position
Trendelenburg position
Prone position with the head turned downwards

questions.rationale: High Fowler's position places the patient in an upright sitting position and may improve lung expansion. Persistent or severe breathlessness requires prompt assessment and appropriate referral rather than positioning alone.

questions.question_text: A nurse is assisting an older patient to move from a bed to a chair. Which action should be performed before the transfer?

choices.text: Assess the patient's strength, balance and ability to follow instructions
Pull the patient quickly by both arms
Place the chair far from the bed
Ask the patient to stand without assistance

questions.rationale: Assessment of strength, balance and mobility helps determine the safest transfer method and level of assistance required. The nurse should prepare the environment, secure the chair and use appropriate body mechanics or transfer equipment.

questions.question_text: A bedridden patient is at risk of developing pressure injuries. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Reposition the patient according to an individualised schedule and inspect pressure areas regularly
Keep the patient in the same position throughout the day
Massage reddened bony prominences vigorously
Place the patient directly on hard surfaces

questions.rationale: Regular repositioning and skin inspection help reduce prolonged pressure and identify early tissue damage. Repositioning frequency should be individualised according to the patient's condition, skin response and support surface.

questions.question_text: A nurse is measuring an adult patient's blood pressure manually. Which procedure helps improve the accuracy of the reading?

choices.text: Use a cuff that is too small for the patient's arm
Allow the patient to rest, support the arm at heart level and use an appropriately sized cuff
Measure immediately after strenuous activity
Place the cuff over thick clothing

questions.rationale: Correct positioning, adequate rest and appropriate cuff size are essential for accurate blood pressure measurement. Incorrect technique can produce misleading readings and affect clinical decisions.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse records an adult patient's temperature as 38.8°C. What does this finding indicate?

choices.text: Hypothermia
Pyrexia
Bradycardia
Hypotension

questions.rationale: A temperature of 38.8°C indicates an elevated body temperature consistent with fever. The nurse should assess associated symptoms, other vital signs and possible causes, including common infections such as malaria.

questions.question_text: A patient with suspected pneumonia has a respiratory rate of 32 breaths per minute and complains of severe breathlessness. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Advise the patient to sleep and return the next day
Assess respiratory status immediately and arrange urgent referral
Encourage the patient to walk around
Give a large meal before further assessment

questions.rationale: Marked tachypnoea with severe breathlessness may indicate significant respiratory compromise. Immediate assessment of airway, breathing, oxygen saturation and other vital signs is necessary while arranging urgent clinical care.

questions.question_text: A nurse is counting the respiratory rate of an adult patient. Which technique is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ask the patient to breathe as quickly as possible
Observe chest or abdominal movements and count respirations for an appropriate period
Count only when the patient is speaking
Estimate the respiratory rate from the patient's pulse

questions.rationale: Respiratory rate is assessed by observing the rise and fall of the chest or abdomen. The nurse should avoid unnecessarily drawing attention to the counting because this may alter the patient's breathing pattern.

questions.question_text: A patient with limited mobility requires a bed bath. Which action should the nurse take to maintain the patient's dignity?

choices.text: Expose the entire body throughout the procedure
Explain the procedure, obtain consent and expose only the area being washed
Allow other household members to observe without permission
Complete the procedure without informing the patient

questions.rationale: Explaining the procedure and obtaining consent promote patient autonomy and cooperation. Maintaining privacy and covering areas not being washed preserve dignity and reduce unnecessary exposure.

questions.question_text: A caregiver asks how to provide oral care for a conscious patient who is unable to brush their teeth independently. Which instruction is most appropriate?

choices.text: Assist with brushing using a soft toothbrush and appropriate positioning
Avoid oral hygiene until the patient can brush independently
Use sharp instruments to remove food particles
Pour large amounts of water into the patient's mouth

questions.rationale: Assisted oral hygiene helps prevent dental disease, oral discomfort and accumulation of microorganisms. Safe positioning and attention to swallowing ability reduce the risk of aspiration.

questions.question_text: A bedridden patient has dry, cracked skin on the lower legs. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Apply an appropriate moisturising product after gentle cleansing
Scrub the skin vigorously with a rough material
Use concentrated disinfectant on the dry skin
Avoid all skin assessment

questions.rationale: Gentle cleansing and appropriate moisturising help maintain skin hydration and reduce cracking. The nurse should also assess for wounds, infection and circulation problems, particularly in patients with diabetes.

questions.question_text: A patient with a prescribed nasogastric feeding regimen is about to receive a feed at home. Which action is essential before administering the feed?

choices.text: Confirm correct tube position using the approved procedure and verify that feeding is prescribed
Assume that the tube is correctly positioned because it was inserted previously
Inject air and rely only on listening over the stomach for confirmation
Administer the feed regardless of the patient's condition

questions.rationale: Incorrect nasogastric tube placement can result in feed entering the respiratory tract and causing serious harm. Tube position must be confirmed using an approved method, such as gastric aspirate pH testing or radiography when indicated, before feeding.

questions.question_text: A patient with difficulty swallowing is being assisted with oral feeding. Which action best reduces the risk of aspiration?

choices.text: Feed the patient while lying flat
Position the patient upright and follow the recommended swallowing and feeding plan
Give large mouthfuls to shorten feeding time
Encourage the patient to talk continuously while swallowing

questions.rationale: Upright positioning and appropriate feeding techniques help reduce the risk of aspiration in patients with dysphagia. The nurse should follow the prescribed swallowing assessment and texture recommendations and stop feeding if signs of aspiration occur.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving nasogastric feeding begins coughing and develops respiratory distress during administration. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Increase the feeding rate
Stop the feed immediately and assess the patient's airway and breathing
Flush the tube with a large volume of water
Continue feeding while asking the patient to cough

questions.rationale: Coughing and respiratory distress during feeding may indicate aspiration or tube displacement. The feed must be stopped immediately, airway and breathing assessed, and urgent clinical assistance obtained as required.

questions.question_text: A female patient confined to bed requests assistance to pass urine. Which action should the nurse take?

choices.text: Provide a suitable bedpan, maintain privacy and assist with positioning
Ask the patient to walk to the toilet regardless of mobility
Insert a urinary catheter without assessment
Restrict fluids to prevent urination

questions.rationale: A bedpan allows a patient who cannot safely access a toilet to pass urine or stool while in bed. Privacy, correct positioning, hand hygiene and safe disposal of waste should be maintained.

questions.question_text: A patient has an indwelling urinary catheter connected to a drainage bag. Which nursing action helps prevent catheter-associated urinary tract infection?

choices.text: Keep the drainage bag below bladder level and maintain a closed drainage system
Disconnect the drainage tubing frequently
Place the drainage bag on the patient's abdomen
Allow the drainage outlet to touch the floor

questions.rationale: Keeping the drainage bag below bladder level helps prevent urine from flowing backwards into the bladder. Maintaining a closed drainage system and appropriate catheter hygiene reduces infection risk.

questions.question_text: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter has had no urine output for three hours. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Remove the catheter immediately without assessment
Check for kinks, compression or obstruction in the drainage tubing and assess the patient
Raise the drainage bag above bladder level
Flush the catheter with any available fluid

questions.rationale: Absent urine output may result from kinked or obstructed tubing, catheter displacement or reduced urine production. The nurse should inspect the drainage system and assess the patient's condition before escalating for clinical review.

questions.topic: Admission and Discharge Procedures in Community Care
questions.question_text: A patient is discharged from a district hospital after treatment for hypertension. Which action by the community health nurse best supports continuity of care?

choices.text: Review the discharge instructions, medication plan and follow-up arrangements with the patient
Tell the patient to stop medication when symptoms disappear
Ignore the discharge summary
Advise the patient to attend follow-up only when severe symptoms occur

questions.rationale: Reviewing the discharge plan helps ensure that the patient understands prescribed treatment, warning signs and follow-up requirements. This supports continuity between hospital-based and community-based healthcare.

questions.topic: Admission and Discharge Procedures in Community Care
questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse receives a patient who has been referred from a CHPS compound to a district hospital. Which information is most important to review?

choices.text: The patient's favourite recreational activity
The reason for referral, assessment findings, treatment already given and relevant patient history
The personal opinions of unrelated community members
The patient's household entertainment preferences

questions.rationale: Referral information should communicate the clinical reason for transfer, relevant findings, interventions and patient history. Accurate information supports appropriate assessment and reduces unnecessary delays in care.

questions.topic: Infection Prevention and Control at Home
questions.question_text: A community health nurse is caring for a patient with a draining wound at home. Which action is most appropriate when removing the used dressing?

choices.text: Wear appropriate gloves, remove the dressing carefully and dispose of it safely
Handle the contaminated dressing with bare hands
Place the dressing on the patient's bed for later disposal
Reuse the dressing if it is not completely soaked

questions.rationale: Used wound dressings may contain blood, body fluids and microorganisms, creating an infection risk. Appropriate personal protective equipment, hand hygiene and safe waste disposal reduce exposure and cross-contamination.

questions.topic: Infection Prevention and Control at Home
questions.question_text: A caregiver accidentally sustains a needlestick injury while cleaning up after a patient's injection. What should the caregiver do immediately?

choices.text: Wash the affected area with soap and running water and seek urgent occupational or clinical assessment
Squeeze the wound aggressively and apply bleach
Ignore the injury if there is no visible bleeding
Cover the injury and wait several weeks before reporting it

questions.rationale: A needlestick injury may expose the individual to blood-borne pathogens such as hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV. Immediate washing and urgent assessment are necessary to determine exposure risk and whether post-exposure management is indicated.

questions.topic: Infection Prevention and Control at Home
questions.question_text: A family is caring for a relative with pulmonary tuberculosis at home. Which instruction is most appropriate?

choices.text: Keep windows closed at all times
Promote good ventilation, respiratory hygiene and adherence to prescribed tuberculosis treatment
Share eating utensils without washing them
Stop treatment once the cough improves

questions.rationale: Pulmonary tuberculosis is transmitted mainly through airborne particles, so good ventilation and respiratory hygiene are important. Adherence to effective treatment and guidance from the tuberculosis control programme help reduce transmission.

questions.question_text: A patient has a minor superficial wound on the forearm. Which procedure is most appropriate during basic wound care?

choices.text: Clean the wound using an appropriate technique and cover it with a suitable dressing
Apply soil to encourage clotting
Pour household bleach directly into the wound
Leave the wound contaminated and uncovered

questions.rationale: Appropriate wound cleansing helps remove contaminants and reduce infection risk. A suitable dressing protects the wound while allowing the healing process to continue.

questions.question_text: A nurse observes redness, warmth, swelling and purulent discharge around a patient's wound during a home visit. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Assess the wound and arrange prompt clinical evaluation
Massage the wound vigorously
Ignore the discharge if the patient has no pain
Apply an unprescribed antibiotic and avoid referral

questions.rationale: Redness, warmth, swelling and purulent discharge are signs suggestive of wound infection. The patient requires clinical assessment to determine the severity and appropriate treatment.

questions.question_text: An older patient reports dizziness when standing from bed. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Encourage the patient to stand quickly
Assist the patient to sit at the bedside before standing and assess for postural hypotension
Advise the patient to walk without support
Keep the patient in a dark room

questions.rationale: Dizziness on standing may indicate postural hypotension and increases the risk of falls. Gradual position changes and assessment of blood pressure and symptoms improve safety.

questions.question_text: A caregiver asks whether an older relative should be restrained to prevent wandering at home. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

choices.text: Recommend routine physical restraints for all older adults
Explain that restraints should not be used routinely and safer alternatives should be assessed first
Advise tying the patient to the bed whenever the caregiver leaves
Use restraints without assessing the patient's condition

questions.rationale: Physical restraints can cause injury, psychological distress and loss of mobility. They should not be used routinely; individual assessment, environmental modifications, supervision and other less restrictive measures should be considered.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a patient's walking path at home is blocked by electrical cables and loose mats. What should the nurse recommend?

choices.text: Leave the items in place because the patient is familiar with the room
Remove or secure the hazards and provide a clear, well-lit walking path
Encourage the patient to walk over the cables carefully
Place additional loose mats along the path

questions.rationale: Loose mats and electrical cables are environmental hazards that increase the risk of falls. Removing or securing them and improving lighting help create a safer home environment.

questions.question_text: A patient with fever becomes confused and has a blood pressure of 84/50 mmHg, pulse rate of 128 beats per minute and respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Provide routine health education and reassess the following day
Recognise possible severe infection with circulatory compromise and arrange emergency referral
Give the patient a large meal
Allow the patient to walk around to improve circulation

questions.rationale: Hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnoea, fever and altered mental status are concerning for sepsis with possible circulatory compromise. Immediate emergency assessment and referral are essential.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving nasogastric feeding suddenly develops coughing, cyanosis and difficulty breathing. Which complication should the nurse suspect first?

choices.text: Aspiration of feed into the respiratory tract
Improved gastric emptying
Normal digestive activity
Mild hunger

questions.rationale: Coughing, cyanosis and respiratory distress during nasogastric feeding are highly concerning for aspiration. Feeding should be stopped immediately and emergency airway and respiratory management initiated.

questions.question_text: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter develops fever, suprapubic discomfort and cloudy, foul-smelling urine. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection
Normal bladder function
Hypoglycaemia
Improved renal function

questions.rationale: Fever and suprapubic discomfort in a catheterised patient may indicate a urinary tract infection. Cloudy or foul-smelling urine alone is insufficient to establish the diagnosis, so clinical assessment and appropriate investigations are required.

questions.question_text: A patient with diabetes has a foot wound with blackened tissue, foul-smelling discharge, fever and increasing pain. Which action should the nurse prioritise?

choices.text: Continue routine dressing changes at home for several weeks
Arrange urgent hospital referral for assessment of severe infection and possible tissue necrosis
Encourage the patient to walk barefoot
Apply herbal preparations and delay medical assessment

questions.rationale: Blackened tissue, foul discharge and fever may indicate tissue necrosis and severe infection, including possible diabetic foot complications. Urgent hospital assessment is required to prevent progression to sepsis or limb-threatening damage.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is attending to three patients at home. Patient A has a minor skin abrasion, Patient B has suddenly become unconscious, and Patient C requires assistance with bathing. Which patient should receive attention first?

choices.text: Patient A
Patient B
Patient C
All patients should receive attention in the order of arrival

questions.rationale: Sudden unconsciousness may indicate a life-threatening emergency involving airway, breathing or circulation. The nurse should assess and support the unconscious patient immediately while arranging emergency assistance.

questions.question_text: A patient has a pulse rate of 46 beats per minute, blood pressure of 88/56 mmHg and reports faintness. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The patient has symptomatic bradycardia with possible haemodynamic compromise
The patient has normal cardiovascular findings
The patient has isolated hypertension
The patient has a normal response to standing

questions.rationale: Bradycardia accompanied by hypotension and faintness may indicate inadequate cardiac output and haemodynamic compromise. The patient requires urgent assessment and clinical intervention.

questions.question_text: A patient recovering from a stroke has right-sided weakness and attempts to walk without assistance. The patient begins to lose balance. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Allow the patient to continue walking to improve confidence
Support the patient to prevent a fall and reassess the need for assistance or mobility aids
Pull the patient forcefully by the affected arm
Ask the patient to move faster

questions.rationale: The immediate priority is to prevent a fall and further injury. The nurse should provide safe support, reassess mobility and use an appropriate transfer or walking aid based on the patient's abilities.

questions.topic: Infection Prevention and Control at Home
questions.question_text: A caregiver is preparing to clean a wound and then prepare food for the family. Which practice is most important to prevent cross-contamination?

choices.text: Perform hand hygiene and safely dispose of contaminated materials before handling food
Use the same gloves for wound care and food preparation
Place used wound dressings on the food preparation surface
Rinse contaminated gloves with water and continue using them

questions.rationale: Wound exudate and used dressings may contain microorganisms that can contaminate food and surfaces. Hand hygiene, appropriate glove removal and safe waste disposal are essential before food handling.

questions.topic: Admission and Discharge Procedures in Community Care
questions.question_text: A patient is discharged after treatment for heart failure. During a follow-up home visit, the nurse finds that the patient has worsening breathlessness, bilateral leg swelling and difficulty lying flat. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Continue routine home monitoring for another month
Recognise possible worsening heart failure and arrange urgent clinical assessment
Advise the patient to increase salt intake
Recommend stopping all prescribed medication

questions.rationale: Worsening breathlessness, peripheral oedema and orthopnoea suggest possible fluid overload and deterioration of heart failure. Prompt clinical assessment is required to prevent further complications.

questions.question_text: A confused older patient repeatedly attempts to leave the house at night. The caregiver asks the nurse to tie the patient to the bed. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Recommend tying the patient securely to prevent movement
Assess the causes of wandering and introduce safer alternatives such as supervision and environmental modifications
Advise the caregiver to lock the patient in a room without supervision
Ignore the behaviour because it is expected in all older adults

questions.rationale: Restraining a confused patient can cause physical injury, psychological distress and further complications. Assessment for reversible causes and safer approaches, including supervision, identification and environmental modifications, should be prioritised.

questions.question_text: A patient sustains a deep wound from a dirty metal object while working on a farm. The wound is contaminated with soil, and the patient's tetanus immunisation history is unknown. What should the nurse prioritise?

choices.text: Apply a dressing and advise the patient to return only if pain develops
Arrange prompt clinical assessment for wound management and tetanus prophylaxis
Apply soil to the wound to stop bleeding
Close the wound at home using ordinary adhesive tape

questions.rationale: A deep, contaminated wound presents a risk of tetanus, particularly when immunisation history is unknown. Prompt clinical assessment is necessary for appropriate wound management and assessment of tetanus vaccine and immunoglobulin requirements.

questions.question_text: A bedridden patient develops sudden severe pain and swelling in one calf. The caregiver reports that the patient has been immobile for several days. Which complication should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Deep vein thrombosis
Simple muscle relaxation
Normal ageing
Oral candidiasis

questions.rationale: Unilateral calf pain and swelling in an immobile patient may indicate deep vein thrombosis. The nurse should arrange urgent medical assessment and avoid massaging the affected leg because of the risk of embolisation.
